questions.q: Which British navigator charted Australia's east coast in 1770?
questions.why: He landed at Botany Bay.

questions.q: In which year did the Australian colonies federate into one nation?
questions.why: Federation took effect on 1 January 1901.

questions.q: For how long have Aboriginal people lived in Australia?
questions.why: They are among the oldest continuous cultures on Earth.

questions.q: Anzac Day remembers the 1915 landing at which place?
questions.why: It is marked every 25 April.

questions.q: Which bushranger wore homemade metal armour in his last stand?
questions.why: He was captured at Glenrowan in 1880.

questions.q: Where did the First Fleet set up a British settlement in 1788?
questions.why: It arrived at Sydney Cove on 26 January 1788.

questions.q: What is 26 January called in Australia?
questions.why: It marks the First Fleet's arrival; many call it Invasion Day.

questions.q: Who was Australia's first Prime Minister?
questions.why: He served from 1901 to 1903.

questions.q: Who commanded the First Fleet and became the first governor of New South Wales?
questions.why: He governed from 1788 to 1792.

questions.q: The Eureka Stockade rebellion of 1854 took place on which goldfield?
questions.why: Miners rebelled against licence fees.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister made the 2008 National Apology to the Stolen Generations?
questions.why: He made it in Parliament on 13 February 2008.

questions.q: Who is Australia's longest-serving Prime Minister?
questions.why: He served over 18 years in total.

questions.q: The 1967 referendum changed the Constitution so Aboriginal people would be counted in what?
questions.why: Over 90% voted yes.

questions.q: In which year did Parliament first sit in Canberra?
questions.why: It met in Melbourne until then.

questions.q: Which Second World War campaign in Papua is famous for its jungle track?
questions.why: Australians fought there in 1942.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister disappeared while swimming in 1967?
questions.why: He vanished off Cheviot Beach, Victoria.

questions.q: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.why: It was chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.q: What is the large sandstone rock in the Northern Territory called?
questions.why: It is sacred to the Anangu people.

questions.q: Which is the world's largest coral reef system?
questions.why: It stretches over 2,300 km off Queensland.

questions.q: Which island state lies south of mainland Australia?
questions.why: Its capital is Hobart.

questions.q: What is Australia's largest city?
questions.why: Melbourne is close behind.

questions.q: What is the capital of Western Australia?
questions.why: It is one of the most isolated big cities in the world.

questions.q: What is the capital of Victoria?
questions.why: It was Australia's capital from 1901 to 1927.

questions.q: What is Australia's longest river?
questions.why: It runs about 2,500 km to South Australia.

questions.q: What is the highest mountain on mainland Australia?
questions.why: It is 2,228 m high, in New South Wales.

questions.q: What is the capital of the Northern Territory?
questions.why: It is named after Charles Darwin.

questions.q: Which is the world's largest sand island?
questions.why: It is off the Queensland coast.

questions.q: Which is Australia's largest state by area?
questions.why: It covers about a third of the country.

questions.q: Which ocean lies to the west of Australia?
questions.why: The Pacific lies to the east.

questions.q: Which sea separates Australia from New Zealand?
questions.why: It is named after Abel Tasman.

questions.q: Which strait separates Tasmania from the mainland?
questions.why: It is about 240 km wide.

questions.q: Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre, Australia's lowest point, is in which state?
questions.why: It only fills with water occasionally.

questions.q: Which horse race is called 'the race that stops the nation'?
questions.why: It is run on the first Tuesday of November.

questions.q: Which cricketer had a Test batting average of 99.94?
questions.why: No one else has averaged over 62 in a long career.

questions.q: Which football code is played on an oval and famous for high marks?
questions.why: The AFL Grand Final is held at the MCG.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics?
questions.why: Melbourne hosted in 1956, and Brisbane will in 2032.

questions.q: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is held in Melbourne?
questions.why: It is the first Grand Slam of each year.

questions.q: Which swimmer was nicknamed the 'Thorpedo'?
questions.why: He won five Olympic gold medals.

questions.q: Rugby league's State of Origin is played between Queensland and which state?
questions.why: Players play for the state where they first played.

questions.q: Which Aboriginal athlete lit the flame and won 400 m gold at Sydney 2000?
questions.why: Over 110,000 people watched her race.

questions.q: Which yacht won the America's Cup for Australia in 1983?
questions.why: It ended the US's 132-year winning streak.

questions.q: Which Australian won Wimbledon in 2021 and the Australian Open in 2022?
questions.why: She retired while world number one.

questions.q: Which cricket ground is known as 'the G'?
questions.why: It holds about 100,000 people.

questions.q: What is Australia's national rugby union team called?
questions.why: The Kangaroos are the rugby league team.

questions.q: Which Australian won the Formula One world championship in 1980?
questions.why: He drove for Williams.

questions.q: Who became Australia's first Formula One world champion, in 1959?
questions.why: In 1966 he won in a car he built himself.

questions.q: Which mare won the Melbourne Cup three years in a row, from 2003 to 2005?
questions.why: No other horse has won it three times.

questions.q: Which Australian has won the most Olympic gold medals?
questions.why: She has won six, all in swimming.

questions.q: Which band recorded 'Highway to Hell'?
questions.why: It was released in 1979.

questions.q: Which Melbourne-born singer had a hit with 'Can't Get You Out of My Head'?
questions.why: It was released in 2001.

questions.q: Which children's TV show is about a blue heeler puppy?
questions.why: It is made in Brisbane.

questions.q: Who starred as Mick Dundee in 'Crocodile Dundee'?
questions.why: It was released in 1986.

questions.q: Which children's band wears coloured skivvies?
questions.why: They formed in Sydney in 1991.

questions.q: Which Australian actor played Wolverine in the X-Men films?
questions.why: He played the role for 17 years.

questions.q: Which Australian actor plays Thor in Marvel films?
questions.why: He first played Thor in 2011.

questions.q: Which long-running soap opera is set on Ramsay Street?
questions.why: It started in 1985.

questions.q: Who directed 'Mad Max'?
questions.why: He also made 'Happy Feet'.

questions.q: Which Adelaide-born singer had a hit with 'Chandelier'?
questions.why: She often performs with her face hidden.

questions.q: Who directed 'Moulin Rouge!' and 'Elvis'?
questions.why: He also made 'Strictly Ballroom'.

questions.q: Which band recorded 'Beds Are Burning'?
questions.why: It calls for land rights for Aboriginal people.

questions.q: Which band had a 1981 hit with 'Down Under'?
questions.why: It became an unofficial anthem for the 1983 America's Cup.

questions.q: Which Banjo Paterson song is called Australia's unofficial anthem?
questions.why: He wrote it in 1895.

questions.q: Which Australian actress won the Best Actress Oscar for 'The Hours'?
questions.why: She played Virginia Woolf.

questions.q: Which Australian author won the Booker Prize twice?
questions.why: For 'Oscar and Lucinda' and 'True History of the Kelly Gang'.

questions.q: Which dark yeast spread is an Australian favourite?
questions.why: It was created in Melbourne in 1922.

questions.q: Which meringue dessert topped with fruit do Australia and New Zealand both claim?
questions.why: It is named after ballerina Anna Pavlova.

questions.q: Which sponge cake is coated in chocolate and coconut?
questions.why: It is said to be named after Lord Lamington.

questions.q: Which oat biscuit is linked to soldiers of the First World War?
questions.why: It keeps well, so it could be posted overseas.

questions.q: What do Australians call a barbecue?
questions.why: 'Arvo' means afternoon.

questions.q: What is an 'esky'?
questions.why: The name comes from a brand.

questions.q: What are 'thongs' in Australian English?
questions.why: They are the summer footwear of choice.

questions.q: Where do Australians famously buy a 'democracy sausage'?
questions.a: At polling places on election day
questions.why: Schools sell them to raise money.

questions.q: Which coin-tossing game may legally be played in pubs on Anzac Day?
questions.why: Soldiers played it in the First World War.

questions.q: Which Sydney festival ends with a parade along Oxford Street?
questions.a: Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras
questions.why: It began in 1978.

questions.q: Which winter festival covers Sydney's buildings in light projections?
questions.why: The Opera House sails are its best-known canvas.

questions.q: What is a 'ute' in Australia?
questions.why: It is short for utility vehicle.

questions.q: Which nut is native to Australia?
questions.why: It grows in Queensland and New South Wales.

questions.q: What does 'bush tucker' mean?
questions.why: It includes wattleseed, finger limes and quandongs.

questions.q: On which day does the Sydney to Hobart Yacht Race start?
questions.why: It covers about 630 nautical miles.

questions.q: Which Hobart festival is held around the winter solstice?
questions.why: It ends with a nude swim in the cold Derwent River.

questions.q: Which bird appears with the kangaroo on Australia's coat of arms?
questions.why: Both are native animals, chosen for the 1912 coat of arms.

questions.q: What is Australia's currency?
questions.why: It replaced the pound in 1966.

questions.q: Which Sydney building has a roof shaped like sails?
questions.why: Danish architect Jørn Utzon designed it.

questions.q: Which egg-laying mammal has a bill like a duck?
questions.why: The echidna also lays eggs.

questions.q: How many states does Australia have?
questions.why: It also has two main mainland territories.

questions.q: Which animal eats eucalyptus leaves and sleeps up to 20 hours a day?
questions.why: Eucalyptus gives it very little energy.

questions.q: What is Australia's national anthem?
questions.why: It became the anthem in 1984.

questions.q: What is Australia's national floral emblem?
questions.why: Its colours inspired the green and gold.

questions.q: Which Australian co-discovered that bacteria cause most stomach ulcers?
questions.why: He shared the 2005 Nobel Prize with Robin Warren.

questions.q: What did Australian scientist David Warren invent?
questions.why: He came up with the idea in the 1950s.

questions.q: What is the upper house of Australia's federal Parliament called?
questions.why: Each state elects 12 senators.

questions.q: Voting in Australian federal elections is what?
questions.why: It has been compulsory since 1924.

questions.q: Hobart is the capital of which state?
questions.why: It is Australia's second-oldest capital.

questions.q: Which Australian helped turn penicillin into a usable medicine?
questions.why: He shared the 1945 Nobel Prize.

questions.q: Which Australian surgeon pioneered the multi-channel cochlear implant?
questions.why: The first one was implanted in 1978.

questions.q: How many points are there on the Commonwealth Star on Australia's flag?
questions.why: Six for the states and one for the territories.
